LESSON: ACCOUNTS OF CREATION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Creation
Topic 2.1: Accounts of Creation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Accounts of Creation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How is the first account of creation different from the second account?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. discuss the similarities and differences between the two accounts of creation
2. identify five attributes of God from the creation accounts
3. value God’s creation by conserving the environment

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: ACCOUNTS OF CREATION
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Accounts of Creation helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: ACCOUNTS OF CREATION
Study Accounts of Creation like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Discuss the similarities and differences between the two accounts of creation

What this means
In this part you learn to discuss the similarities and differences between the two accounts of creation. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: discuss the similarities and differences between the two accounts of creation.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Accounts of Creation” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can discuss the similarities and differences between the two accounts of creation. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Identify five attributes of God from the creation accounts

What this means
In this part you learn to identify five attributes of God from the creation accounts. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify five attributes of God from the creation accounts.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Accounts of Creation in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify five attributes of God from the creation accounts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Value God’s creation by conserving the environment

What this means
In this part you learn to value God’s creation by conserving the environment. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value God’s creation by conserving the environment.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value God’s creation by conserving the environment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Accounts of Creation is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Accounts of Creation” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: discuss the similarities and differences between the two accounts of creation)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Accounts of Creation in your own words. (skill: identify five attributes of God from the creation accounts)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: value God’s creation by conserving the environment)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Accounts of Creation to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: discuss the similarities and differences between the two accounts of creation.
3. Practise this skill: identify five attributes of God from the creation accounts.
4. Practise this skill: value God’s creation by conserving the environment.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Accounts of Creation from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Accounts of Creation: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Accounts of Creation?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How is the first account of creation different from the second account?
2. Why is it important to learn about the creation accounts?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Accounts of Creation means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: discuss the similarities and differences between the two accounts of creation.
5. Be able to: identify five attributes of God from the creation accounts.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
